Thanks — I pulled the annotated inventory. Quick proposal for nodepools based on the workload profiles you sent:

- control-plane: 3 x m6a-like nodes (8 vCPU / 32GB), external etcd, spread across racks for quorum. Taints: node-role.kubernetes.io/control:NoSchedule
- infra (system): 2 x general-purpose (4 vCPU / 16GB) for logging/monitoring/ingress (daemonsets + small stateful sets)
- default-worker-cpu: 6 x worker-cpu (32 vCPU / 128GB) for model preprocess & CPU-bound inference
- gpu-inference: 2 x gpu workers (A100-equivalent / 80GB) initially for batch/low-latency model serving. Auto-scale to 4 with reserved burst capacity and graceful fallback to CPU pool.
- batch-spot: 4 x cheaper spot-like nodes for training jobs and heavy-batch work (evictible).

I put a detailed sizing sheet in the spreadsheet I've attached (k8s-nodepool-sizing.xlsx). Notes:
- We recommend nodeAffinity on the GPU pool to prefer racks with direct NVMe access; tolerate on others.
- For HA: ensure control-plane at least 3 masters across rack boundaries; workers can be zoned with podDisruptionBudgets for critical services.

I'll walk through the sizing in the Tue call if scheduled.

Attachments: k8s-nodepool-sizing.xlsx

Following up with the storage recommendation set after reviewing the inventory and proposed nodepools. High-level: separate three logical tiers on NVMe-backed arrays + object 
store for cold weights.

1) Hot SSD tier (local NVMe):
- Use for model weights that require sub-10ms cold-starts and KV cache.
- StorageClass: local-ssd-scratch (ReadWriteOnce, ephemeral, default TTL 7d for cache).
- Backup cadence: snapshot hourly for weights during deployment windows.

2) Warm SSD tier (shared NVMe via iSCSI or NVMeoF):
- For medium-term artifacts (recent checkpoints). Use a shared CSI driver with ReadWriteMany.
- StorageClass: shared-nvme (replication factor 2 across racks). Snapshot daily.

3) Cold object tier (S3-compatible on-prem object store):
- For archived models and large blobs. Lifecycle to move to offline tape after 90 days.

Additional operational notes:
- Use CSI snapshot + Velero for cluster-level retention; ensure Velero has access to object store.
- SSD-tiering-proposal.pdf has IOPS/kg targets and recommended QoS: HOT= >100k IOPS, WARM=10-30k.
- arch-diagram-v2.png attached with rack placement and preferred NVMe mapping.

On encryption: recommend node-level dm-crypt for local NVMe plus KMS integration with your HSM. We'll need to confirm the KMS endpoint and ACLs during the review.

Attachments: ssd-tiering-proposal.pdf, arch-diagram-v2.png

- KMS endpoint: kms.novamed.local (HSM-backed) — Carlos will provide ACLs prior to Tue.
- Tue 2027-06-15 10:00 PT works for the team. Please include a short slide (5-7) to capture the nodepool plan, affinity rules, and SSD tiering summary.

On the GPU fallback: we want a concrete fallback plan if the GPU pool is saturated — a kube-level graceful-fallback policy and a plan to snapshot in-flight model state to warm tier. Can Marissa propose a fallback sequence in the call?

I'll forward the calendar invite.
